chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Hinton asks what it felt like to be in the Basie rhythm section
summary: Hinton praises the Basie rhythm section of Jones, Page, Green and Basie and asks what it was like inside it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You're just amazing. Just a minute, Jo, I want to get back to something else. I want to ask you - it turns out as time will show and has shown as of 1973, in all the annals of band playing dance music, there's only been one superlative rhythm section, one that was impeccable, that is held in esteem by every jazz musician in the world and every jazz listener, everyone that appreciates jazz, and that was the great rhythm section which you headed in the Count Basie band. That is with you, Jo Jones, on drums; Walter Page, who you say is the daddy and the father of all; Freddie Greene which you say is an annexation of Cliff McTighe and Walter Page the fourth. Count Basie, Walter Page, Jo Jones, and Freddie Greene. In all the annals of the music business and music history in dance playing and time keeping, you four are considered in every way the keepers of time. How did you guys feel? I looked at you and I've listened to your bands...when I was with Cab Calloway... and here I'm listening and looking, and it was just unbelievable. I know what it was like to hear you and listen to and see you guys play and to sit and watch Walter Page, the relaxation of that great rhythm section. But what was it like to be in there with you guys?
ON THE SPIRITUALITY OF PLAYING IN RHYTHM SECTIONS WITH BASIE - "MORAL PERFECTION"
